A 42-year-old male arrives at the emergency department with altered mental status. His medical history
includes liver cirrhosis due to chronic alcoholism. Over the past few days, his confusion has
progressively worsened. His vital signs are as follows: temperature 98.7°F (37.1°C), blood pressure
131/89 mmHg, pulse 73/min, respirations 17/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Physical
examination reveals a non-tender, distended abdomen. Neurological examination shows confusion and
asterixis. Laboratory results are as follows: Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.3 mEq/L
HCO3-: 22 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 59 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL What is
the most appropriate next step in treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Magnesium sulfate
(B) Normal saline (C) Vitamin K (D) Albumin (E) Calcium gluconate (F) Potassium (G) Thiamine (H)
Lactulose (I) Rifaximin (J) Dextrose
